Subject: Q on auto-renew / termination-for-convenience in draft order form

Mina —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Before we get legal involved I wanted to confirm a couple of commercial guardrails so we can scope internal approvals: 1) the order form references an automatic one-year renewal unless we give notice — what is Redwood’s standard notice window today? We were budgeting for 60 days, but the draft language looks like 30 days.

2) We also need clarity on "termination for convenience" language. If Brightway needs to wind down before the term ends, our procurement team needs a predictable fee schedule (we typically ask for a declining fee schedule or a capped percentage of remaining committed spend). Can Redwood share the playbook?

I attached the Brightway PO and the draft order form we received for reference. Happy to hop on a 20-min call this week if that helps.

Thanks,

Evan — thanks for the clear notes and for attaching the PO. Quick answers up front: we can be flexible on the notice window (30 / 45 / 60 days are all in play depending on commitment and billing cadence), and termination-for-convenience is something Legal will want to define with a short fee ladder.

I'm looping in Ben (legal) to propose specific contract language and Laura (your AE) for commercial alignment. Proposed next step: Ben to send a redline with a recommended notice default (we generally prefer 60 days for annual contracts to avoid abrupt downstream infra changes) and a 3-tier termination fee (e.g., 50% / 30% / 10% of remaining committed fees by time-to-term). If Brightway pushes back we can move to a flat cap instead.

If that sounds OK I'll schedule a 30-min call for Friday to walk through options so procurement can surface a preference to your CFO.

Evan / Mina —

Thanks — I reviewed the draft order form and attached an annotated redline (Redline_MSA_12-02.docx) with the recommended language. Summary of our position: 

- Auto-renew: propose mutual automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party provides written notice at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term. The mutual language reduces one-sided churn risk and is standard for our enterprise orders.

- Notice windows: default = 60 days; we can consider a 45-day compromise for pilots or short pilot-to-paid conversions but need 60 days for enterprise annual commitments.

- Termination for convenience (TFC): recommend a time-based tapering fee to mitigate stranded capacity and on-boarding costs: 50% of remaining committed fees if terminated within first 6 months, 30% if between 6–12 months, 10% if after 12 months but before term end. Alternatively we can accept a flat cap at 40% of remaining committed fees if that helps procurement budgeting.

Rationale: the taper balances Brightway flexibility while protecting Redwood from immediate capacity and provisioning costs tied to reserved/dedicated capacity. If Brightway prefers a liquidated-damages style cap, propose the 40% flat cap for simplicity.

Next steps: please review redline and tell us which approach (taper vs flat cap) you prefer. If you want, we can turn our redline into a short addendum that sits on top of the order form so the commercial language is obvious to procurement/legal reviewers.

--
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

Ben / Mina —

Appreciate the clear options and the redline. After internal review Brightway Procurement is prepared to accept the 60-day mutual notice default and the tapering TFC schedule, but we have one commercial ask: could you cap the maximum termination-for-convenience exposure at 30% of remaining committed fees (i.e., even if terminated in month 1, the maximum we would owe is 30%)? Our CFO will not approve anything above a single-digit to low double-digit cap without an executive waiver.

If Redwood can't accept a hard 30% cap, we would prefer the flat 40% cap (Ben's alt) over a higher tapered 50% at month zero. We are aiming to finalize commercial terms this week so we can route back to legal and get e-signature.

If you're able to accept 30% cap I'll circulate the updated PO and ask for a DocuSign flow. If not, let me know and we can discuss tradeoffs (e.g., removing mutual auto-renew or shortening notice window in exchange for lower TFC exposure).

Thanks,
Evan Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Brightway Inc.

Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround. I ran this with Finance and Legal and here's a pragmatic path that should keep the CF folks happy while protecting Redwood:

- We will convert Ben's redline into a two-line addendum (TFC: \"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor's aggregate liability for termination for convenience shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the remaining committed fees as of the effective date of termination.\") and attach it to the order form.
